audit.summary: The published gradient can increase its stated objective; the stability proof does not justify an iteration-independent bound; the printed reward reverses its released implementation; the released RL path fails its perturbation cap; and two metric pairs are impossible under the stated definitions.
limitations: Limitations: No author code, datasets, weights or original experiments were executed.
Limitations: Repository bytes are a pinned later public commit, not established experiment provenance.
Limitations: Separate OpenReview supplement access was blocked in source preparation; embedded appendices were available.

Limitations: Theorem 6.3's literal all-real-weights eigengap premise is infeasible; the stability counterexample is explicitly to the meaningful simplex/squared-mixture interpretation, not a false claim to satisfy that literal premise.
Limitations: No full benchmark rerun or exhaustive audit of all clustering baselines; later errata search limited to publisher and repository landing pages.

P1 — Gradient inconsistent with the defined linear kernel mixture — Counterevidence: Appendix Eq25 uses squared weights, suggesting intended alternative. A.1 also adds the top-eigenspace term where subtraction is required. No claim all empirical algorithms use this derivation.

P2 — Iteration-independent stability is not obtained from the recurrence — Counterevidence: Hidden constants could depend on a prescribed finite T; then the weaker statement is not refuted. Literal impossible premise is not claimed satisfied.
P3 — Printed reward promotes original-cluster similarity — Counterevidence: Released ClusterEnv and critic both use 1-inter_metric; historical runs may therefore use the intended attack direction.

P4 — Released RL path does not enforce the perturbation budget — Counterevidence: Alternate optimization path normalizes; soft mean penalty does not cap sampled cumulative noise. Exact historical table-generating code unknown.

P5 — Two accuracy/purity pairs cannot share the stated metric definitions — Counterevidence: Different unmatched aggregations could evade paired inequality but are not disclosed and require clarification. Two-decimal rounding cannot explain gaps.

assumptions: Two unit-diagonal PSD 2x2 kernels; K=1; simplex gamma; /N normalization; nonzero uniform feasible eigengap.
Counterexample explicitly uses the natural feasible-simplex and squared-mixture reading; literal all-real gamma premise is impossible at zero.
Two orthonormal-column N=4,K=2 representations and original two-cluster co-occurrence; no full constrained-data attack asserted.
Single environment, reset cumulative noise, positive threshold, sampled action with norm above radius; Gaussian policy has full support.
Same samples/predictions or paired-run averages; one-to-one mapped accuracy and per-cluster majority purity.
